title: Case Study: 6-Year Backtest & Forward-Test Results for an Automated Option Selling Strategy
author: Certain_Pipe1889
selftext:
​

After five months of refining my approach, I finalized a parameter structure designed to adapt across different market regimes without requiring year-over-year adjustments.

 Transitioning from manual execution to a simplified option selling algorithm improved live performance while maintaining strict risk controls. Over a 6-year backtest (August 2020 to present), the maximum drawdown was capped at 11% of capital, inclusive of realistic slippage and transaction costs.

Statistical Profile & Trade Mechanics

The core edge relies on asymmetrical risk-reward rather than a high win rate:

 \* Win Rate: \~37% (expecting a higher frequency of smaller loss days).

 \* Payoff Ratio: Average winner is 1.7x the size of an average loss.

 \* Edge: Combining a 1:1.7 risk-reward profile with the natural probability decay of option selling provides consistent expectancy over time.

Infrastructure & Execution Pipeline

Coming from a non-engineering background, I spent two months prompt-engineering with cloud AI models to develop and refine the codebase (with major assistance from my dad on the technical logic).

 \* Hosting: Deployed on an AWS Mumbai instance for low-latency broker API execution.

 \* Automation: Fully hands-off. The script initiates automatically before market open (8:45 AM), handles entries/exits dynamically, and closes at pre-set conditions.

 \* Calendar Logic: Pre-programmed with market holiday schedules and weekends to handle non-trading days automatically.
